# Security policy — JFH-CODE experimental beta

**Do not execute untrusted JFH-CODE.** JavaScript generated by JFH-CODE runs with ordinary Node.js host privileges. M8's execution budget and recursion limit are **not a security sandbox**; they do not prevent filesystem/network access or all denial-of-service behaviors.

JFH-CODE Studio is a **single-user, localhost-only** development tool. Do not expose it through a reverse proxy, tunnel, publicly reachable IP, shared computer, or cloud service. There has been no independent security audit. Use a disposable or least-privileged development environment when experimenting.

The optional OpenAI API key is provided by the user, separately billed and held in Studio's server process memory. Never commit or paste genuine keys, passwords or private data into issues, patches, tests or source files.

Please report vulnerabilities **privately** through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, if enabled, or contact https://www.fastsell.net/. Do not publish working exploits before maintainers can respond. There is no guaranteed support or patch SLA during beta.
